strategy.summary: Reproduce the numerical correctness failure in `cvxpy.atoms.suppfunc.SuppFuncAtom._value_impl` where an internal support-function solve path uses SCS with a hardcoded `eps=1e-6`, causing the test to fail by a small margin (≈1.5707e-06 > 1e-6) when using SCS 3.3.1 and NumPy/SciPy versions at/above those validated in PR#3513.

pinned_because: scs: The documented failure mode is specifically associated with SCS 3.3.1, and the project declares `scs >= 3.2.4.post1`; reproducing the latent accuracy difference requires installing/using the SCS version that exhibits it.

numpy/scipy: PR#3513 validation mentions NumPy 2.4.6 and SciPy 1.17.1; using sufficiently new versions consistent with the validated environment helps ensure the same numerical conditioning/solver behavior.
Clarabel: Tests/paths may switch solvers in other parts of the suite; ensuring Clarabel is installed prevents unrelated skips/errors and matches the documented dependency set.

strategy.reproducing_test: Run the specific support-function related test(s) that exercise `SuppFuncAtom._value_impl` and compare the computed value against the analytic support-function within an absolute tolerance of 1e-6 (as reported in issue#3514). If multiple tests match, narrow further by running `pytest -q cvxpy/tests -k "SuppFuncAtom or suppfunc"`.
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision `a4b9e106004c`, executing the support-function test(s) causes an assertion failure of the form `abs(actual - expected) <= 1e-6` because the internal SCS call returns an error ≈1.5707e-06 (with SCS 3.3.1). On the fixed revision (PR#3513 intended fix), the same test(s) pass because the support-function numerical evaluation no longer suffers that hardcoded/insufficient SCS tolerance behavior (e.g., tightened/changed solver strategy such that the error drops to ~1e-10 range when using an effectively smaller eps, or equivalent improved accuracy).
strategy.numerical_probe: Not required for grading; the failing test itself is the oracle. Internally, the bug is attributed to `SuppFuncAtom._value_impl` calling `prob.solve(solver='SCS', eps=1e-6)` and returning a value whose analytic error can be ≈1.5707e-06 under SCS 3.3.1. The transition to success is when that test no longer detects the >1e-6 discrepancy.

input_output_examples.input: Support function evaluation in `SuppFuncAtom._value_impl` where it calls `prob.solve(solver='SCS', eps=1e-6)`
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Failure occurs with `abs(actual - expected) = 1.5707e-06` under the failing configuration; the test asserts `abs(actual - expected) <= 1e-6`.
input_output_examples.expected_output: The test passes with `abs(actual - expected) <= 1e-6`. (In the reported investigation, changing eps to `1e-8` reduces the error to `1.7e-10`.)

risks: This is solver-version sensitive: the failure is reported to occur with SCS 3.3.1; if SCS is upgraded/downgraded relative to the failing version, the discrepancy may disappear and the test may pass on the buggy revision.

The exact failing test name/line is not included in the provided evidence. The reproduction must therefore first locate the relevant test(s) under `cvxpy/tests` that cover `SuppFuncAtom._value_impl` and perform the `<= 1e-6` analytic comparison.

If you run a suite or select a test subset that routes support-function evaluation through a different solver (e.g., via CLARABEL), the SCS-specific hardcoded-eps bug may not manifest; ensure the support-function test uses the internal SCS evaluation path rather than overriding it.

CI platform/architecture and BLAS/LAPACK implementations can change numerical results slightly; this bug is close to the threshold (≈1.57e-6 vs 1e-6), so small numeric drift could flip pass/fail even with the same versions.

oracle.reference_source: Analytic support-function value used by the test (issue#3514 reports the test asserts `abs(actual - expected) <= 1e-6`).
oracle.why: The evidence states the test fails because the returned value differs from the analytic value by ≈1.5707e-06, exceeding the fixed absolute tolerance bound of 1e-6. The fixed revision should bring the error well below that bound (reported to ~1.7e-10 when using eps=1e-8).

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The support-function test assertion observes `abs(actual - expected) ≈ 1.5707e-06`, so `assert abs(actual - expected) <= 1e-6` fails on `a4b9e106004c` when SCS 3.3.1 is installed and the internal SCS solve uses `eps=1e-6`.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After applying the PR#3513 fix (fixed revision corresponding to that PR), the same support-function test(s) pass because the computed support-function value error is reduced to <=1e-6 (reported improvement when using a tighter eps, e.g. 1e-8, yields error ≈1.7e-10).
